      <h1>Orchestration Topology Selector: Which Patterns Do We Sanction?</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A sanctioned-topology table: work class, topology, recursion depth, max fan-out, and enforcing harness — the reference architecture for how your organisation runs agents.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-17-orchestration-topology-selector</b><br>
      Pack D - Architecture and ownership<br>
      fill order <b>6</b> &middot; type <b>decision</b><br>

    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Use one copy of Block A for each class of work your organisation does. Select its sanctioned topology, declare recursion depth and maximum fan-out, mark whether both bounds are declared at the dispatch site, and name the harness that enforces them. Use one copy of Block C for each intended agent workflow. Complete Block D only when a sanctioned topology uses Panel. Fill the topology-specific instantiation page for each topology you sanction.

  <div class="ws-source">

    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch17-multi-agent-orchestration.html#sec-multi-agent-specialization">#sec-multi-agent-specialization</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Read the reference. Use the topology pages later in this packet to record your organisation's instantiation for each topology you sanction.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Three specialization patterns
      <span class="ws-block-note">reference diagrams</span></h2>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:2mm;font-size:8pt">
      <div style="border:0.4mm solid #73808c;padding:2mm">
        <b>Writer / Reviewer / Tester</b><br>
        Writer agent &rarr; <i>code changes</i> &rarr; Reviewer agent &rarr;
        <i>findings: bugs, logic errors, security</i> &rarr; Tester agent &rarr;
        <i>test updates + verification</i> &rarr; Verified output
      </div>
      <div style="border:0.4mm solid #73808c;padding:2mm">
        <b>Domain Teams</b><br>
        Architecture team: type definitions, module boundaries, pattern catalog, dependency graph
        &nbsp;&nbsp; | &nbsp;&nbsp;
        Domain expert team: output conventions, symbol dictionaries, UX guidelines, migration patterns.
        Each team owns its concern and its related files.
      </div>
      <div style="border:0.4mm solid #73808c;padding:2mm">
        <b>Audit / Execute / Validate</b><br>
        Audit agents (read-only) &rarr; <i>findings: files, severity, recommendations</i> &rarr;
        Planning (human decision) &rarr; <i>scoped tasks with file assignments</i> &rarr;
        Execution agents (read-write) &rarr; <i>code changes</i> &rarr;
        Validation agents (read-only) &rarr; <i>review findings, test results</i> &rarr; Ship
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Block B — topology reference
      <span class="ws-block-note">printed, read-only except column 14 on topology pages</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:6%"><col style="width:22%"><col style="width:36%"><col style="width:36%">

      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">10</span></td>
          <td><b>Topology</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Single agent / Writer-Reviewer-Tester / Domain Teams / Audit-Execute-Validate<span class="prior-src">ch17 L56, L75, L134</span></td>
          <td class="locked">Printed reference. Read; do not fill.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">11</span></td>
          <td><b>Stages, and what passes between them</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Writer-Reviewer-Tester — Writer agent &rarr; code changes &rarr; Reviewer agent &rarr; findings: bugs, logic errors, security &rarr; Tester agent &rarr; test updates + verification &rarr; Verified output.<br><br>
            Audit-Execute-Validate — Audit agents (read-only) &rarr; findings: files, severity, recommendations &rarr; Planning (human decision) &rarr; scoped tasks with file assignments &rarr; Execution agents (read-write) &rarr; code changes &rarr; Validation agents (read-only) &rarr; review findings, test results &rarr; Ship.<br><br>
            Domain Teams — parallel teams, each owning a concern and every file related to it; the pattern scales by adding a team per concern.<br><br>
            Single agent — no stages.<span class="prior-src">ch17 L65-68, L139-152, L77-86</span></td>
          <td class="locked">Printed reference. Read; do not fill.</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch17-multi-agent-specialization.html#sec-multi-agent-specialization">#sec-multi-agent-specialization</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Read the reference. The stage boundary and ownership details are printed so your team can point to the constraint it intends to preserve.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Block B — topology reference (continued)
      <span class="ws-block-note">printed, read-only except column 14 on topology pages</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:6%"><col style="width:22%"><col style="width:36%"><col style="width:36%">
      </colgroup>
      <thead>
        <tr><th></th><th>Field</th><th>What the book says</th><th>Your answer</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">12</span></td>
          <td><b>The constraint that makes the topology work</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Writer-Reviewer-Tester — the reviewer receives the diff plus the original source, not the writer's conversation history, so it evaluates the output on its own merits rather than being anchored by the writer's reasoning.<br><br>
            Audit-Execute-Validate — audit and validation agents are read-only and can therefore be dispatched in parallel over the same files with no risk of interference; only execution agents hold write, and the human decision between audit and execution is the highest-impact point in the process.<br><br>
            Domain Teams — neither team needs the other's context; the coordination cost is between teams, not within them.<span class="prior-src">ch17 L73, L154-156, L84-86</span></td>
          <td class="locked">Printed reference. Read; do not fill.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">13</span></td>
          <td><b>Domain Teams reference split</b></td>
          <td class="prior"><b>Architecture team</b> — context loaded: type definitions, module boundaries, pattern catalogue, dependency graph. Owns: type-safety fixes, dead-code removal, API consolidation.<br><br>
            <b>Domain expert team</b> — context loaded: output conventions, symbol dictionaries, UX guidelines, migration patterns. Owns: verbose coverage, logger migration, formatting cleanup.<span class="prior-src">ch17 L79-82</span></td>
          <td class="locked">Printed reference. Read; do not fill.</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
